albums.blurb: Yasmin Williams is a fingerstyle guitarist from northern Virginia with an unusual technique: she often lays the guitar flat on her lap and taps with both hands, sometimes setting a kalimba on top of the strings or wearing tap shoes for percussion. Urban Driftwood, released on the Spinster label, is her second album after the self-released Unwind (2018); it was written during 2020, and kora player Amadou Kouyate guests on the title track. The whole record is instrumental — solo guitar at its core, with folk and West African rhythmic threads.
albums.reception: Urban Driftwood was named one of NPR Music's 50 Best Albums of 2021.

albums.blurb: Men I Trust are a self-produced band from Quebec built around Emmanuelle Proulx's hushed vocals and Jessy Caron's melodic bass lines. Oncle Jazz is their third album and their biggest statement: a 24-track, 71-minute set released independently in September 2019, folding earlier standalone singles like Show Me How and Tailwhip into a long, low-lit sequence of soft-focus grooves. It's the album that preceded Untourable Album (2021).
albums.reception: Oncle Jazz was longlisted for the 2020 Polaris Music Prize, the annual award for the best Canadian album.

albums.blurb: Billy Strings, born William Apostol in Michigan, was raised on traditional bluegrass by his stepfather and grew into one of the fastest flatpickers of his generation, known for stretching the form toward psychedelic, jam-band territory. Home, released on Rounder Records in 2019, is his second studio album after Turmoil & Tinfoil (2017) and the record that broke him to a national audience, mixing tight traditional picking with darker songwriting about addiction and his hometown.
albums.reception: Home won Best Bluegrass Album at the 63rd Grammy Awards and spent 77 weeks on Billboard's Bluegrass Albums chart, reaching No. 1.
